correctness.rationale: Under a real/complex n×2 Gaussian matrix G, U=G(G*G)^(-1/2) is exactly Haar Stiefel and edge length ell_i=||U_i||², sum ell_i=2. With S=G*G/n, n ell_i=G_i S^-1 G_i*: a fixed-dimensional covariance tail gives uniformly over all i (1−δ)T_i≤n ell_i≤(1+δ)T_i, δ=O(sqrt(log n/n)) with exceptional O(n^-3). The T_i are iid χ²_2 (real) or Gamma(2,1) (complex). Their minimum and maximum exact joint CDF [F(b)−F(a)]^n proves planar Exp/Gumbel and spatial Rayleigh/Gumbel independence, with the claimed scales. Disjoint rare small/large bins give independent marked PPP Laplace functionals; simultaneous sandwich transfers under vague convergence. Differentiating F at a=O(1/n) or O(1/sqrt n) and b≈log n bounds the compact-threshold joint comparison by O_R((log n)^{3/2}/sqrt n). Independent real/complex polar-factor constructions checked frame identities and simultaneous inequalities, not asymptotic limits.

originality.rationale: Cantarella–Deguchi–Shonkwiler 2012 defines exactly these quaternionic/Hopf Haar polygon measures, gives single-edge beta marginals and explicitly assumes edge independence only for an approximation in its Section 11. Neither that assumption nor marginal beta laws proves the two-sided joint marked Poisson law. Kabluchko–Prochno 2022 studies random Stiefel large deviations at a different speed; its theorem statement does not imply the extreme rare-bin law or compact-threshold rate. Equivalent projector diagonal leverage scores were searched. PASS with residual potential unindexed projector-extrema theorem.
